summary: Full backend + frontend validation of the new PHASE 8 'Multi-Horizon Desk' feature. ALL 6 review-request checks PASS. (1) Unit tests: `pytest tests/test_timeframes.py -q` → 6/6 pass (parses all three horizons, clamps confidence & maps invalid decision→HOLD, missing horizon→None, garbage/empty/`{}`→None, fallback never invents prices, fallback handles empty verdict). (2) Full backend suite: `pytest tests/ -q` → 63/63 pass in 73s. (3) E2E new phase (test_e2e_timeframes.py, 9/9 pass in 33s against the public preview URL): POST /api/analyze {AAPL} → polled GET /api/analysis/{id} to status=completed; confirmed `total_steps==13`, `len(messages)==13`, last message's agent == 'Multi-Horizon Desk'; top-level `timeframes` object contains short_term/medium_term/long_term, each with decision∈{BUY,SELL,HOLD}, integer confidence 0-100, target_price/stop_loss (number|null), thesis (string|null), horizon, and non-empty label; existing `verdict` object still exposes decision/confidence/target_price/stop_loss/summary/key_risks/time_horizon; `debate` object still present. Live LLM output on this run was short=HOLD(86%,$344.57/$320)/med=BUY(68%,$360/$316)/long=BUY(78%,$372/$302) — per the agent-to-agent note, mixed calls across horizons are the point of the feature, not a bug. (4) Non-regression endpoints: /api/quote/AAPL, /api/chart/AAPL?range=1M, /api/ohlc/RELIANCE.NS?range=1M, /api/news/AAPL all return 200. (5) FRONTEND TimeframesCard on 390x844 viewport at /analysis/7942ab3f-0ced-4ccd-aef0-013531c881b2: tapped tab-segment-verdict → scrolled to testID `timeframes-card`; header 'MULTI-HORIZON VIEW' visible; three tabs labelled '1-2 WEEKS', '1-3 MONTHS', '6-12 MONTHS' each show their decision (HOLD/BUY/BUY on this run); default (short_term) body shows decision badge + '86% CONFIDENCE' + thesis + TARGET $344.57 / STOP LOSS $320.00; tapping '6-12 MONTHS' swapped body to BUY/78%/$372/$302 with the long-term thesis, then tapping '1-3 MONTHS' swapped again to BUY/68%/$360/$316 — three distinct body renderings confirmed. (6) Non-regression on same screen: GroundingBadge (grounding-badge), PositionSizer (position-sizer), VerdictLevels (verdict-levels), Fear & Greed (fear-greed-gauge), LATEST HEADLINES and the price chart (19 svg/canvas elements) all render; DOM geometry confirms TimeframesCard sits directly below PositionSizer (position-sizer bottom=585px, timeframes-card top=597px); no red-screen error overlay; only console warnings are innocuous (RN-web `props.pointerEvents is deprecated` and an iframe-sandbox notice from the preview shell). Result: feature is production-ready as spec'd.
critical_code_review_comments: TimeframesCard tabs (Pressable) do NOT expose per-tab testIDs; only the card container has testID='timeframes-card'. Playwright selected them by visible text ('1-2 WEEKS' / '1-3 MONTHS' / '6-12 MONTHS'), which worked, but for regression stability consider adding testID='timeframe-tab-short'/'-medium'/'-long' (see /app/frontend/src/components/TimeframesCard.tsx:40-49). Non-blocking.

TimeframesCard fallback-detection uses substring match `call.thesis?.toLowerCase().includes('unavailable')` on the thesis string (line 27). A legitimate LLM thesis that happens to contain the word 'unavailable' (e.g. 'liquidity is unavailable at the option strike') would trigger the fallback note. Consider carrying an explicit `is_fallback: bool` flag through parse_timeframes/fallback_timeframes and reading that instead of scanning text.

server.parse_timeframes/fallback_timeframes: no direct issues found; behavior matches the 6 unit tests and matches the spec (fallback reuses primary verdict's decision/confidence, leaves target/stop null, thesis contains 'unavailable'). The additive `timeframes` field on the analysis document is stored via `$set` and does not break any existing endpoint or shape (verified via GET /api/analysis/{id}).
